title: Why it's wrong to look at work-life balance as an achievement ｜ 为什么把工作与生活的平衡视为一种成就是错误的

sents.en: Few topics have been so endlessly analysed as work-life balance.
sents.cn: 很少有话题像工作与生活的平衡这样被无休止地剖析。

sents.en: The quest to attain this mysterious state has dominated discussion around careers for years·especially for working parents.
sents.cn: 多年来，对这种神秘状态的追求主导了围绕职业的讨论——尤其是对有工作的父母而言。

sents.en: The concept is often presented as something to achieve, or a goal to reach.
sents.cn: 这一概念常被呈现为某种需要达成的东西，或一个要达到的目标。

sents.en: And once you've reached it, congratulations: you've made it; you're a successful human being of the 21st century.
sents.cn: 而一旦你达到了，恭喜：你成功了；你是21世纪成功的人。

sents.en: But the problem is that we often tell ourselves: "I'm going to put in eight hours' worth of work, and then I'm going to put in eight hours' worth of 'me time', which will include my family, my hobbies, my workout, my everything," says Anat Lechner, clinical associate professor of management at New York University.
sents.cn: 但问题在于，我们常这样告诉自己："我要投入相当于八小时的工作，然后投入相当于八小时的'自我时间'，其中包括家人、爱好、锻炼，我的一切，"纽约大学管理学临床副教授阿纳特∙莱希纳说。

sents.en: "I don't think it's such a simple formula."
sents.cn: "我不认为这是如此简单的公式。"

sents.en: And, according to new findings, it may not be.
sents.cn: 而根据新的研究发现，它或许并非如此简单。

sents.en: Some researchers are now encouraging us to stop thinking about work-life balance as an achievement that you either hit or don't.
sents.cn: 一些研究者如今鼓励我们停止把工作与生活的平衡看作一种要么达成、要么未达成的成就。

sents.en: Instead, they suggest it may be more of a lifelong process·a continuous, never-ending exercise that requires self-awareness and timely adjustments.
sents.cn: 相反，他们认为它更像是一种终身过程——一种持续的、永无止境的练习，需要自我觉察与及时的调整。

sents.en: Researchers Ioana Lupu and Mayra Ruiz-Castro argue that work-life balance is "a cycle, not an achievement" In their 2020 study, the researchers interviewed nearly 80 employees at two London-based firms·an equal number of men and women between the ages of 30 and 50, all with at least one dependent child·who worked in middle or senior management roles.
sents.cn: 研究者约安娜∙卢普和迈拉∙鲁伊斯-卡斯特罗认为，工作与生活的平衡是"一个循环，而非一项成就"。在她们2020年的研究中，研究者采访了伦敦两家公司的近80名员工——男女人数相等，年龄在30至50岁之间，均至少抚养一个子女——他们担任中层或高层管理职务

sents.en: Although it sounds like the respondents had a lot in common, here's what separated them: about 30% of the men and 50% of the Women reported resisting working long hours.
sents.cn: 尽管听起来受访者有许多共同点，但区分他们的是：约30%的男性和50%的女性表示抗拒长时间工作。

sents.en: The other respondents, meanwhile, all worked long hours because they thought that's what successful professionals should do.
sents.cn: 而其余的受访者则都长时间工作，因为他们认为成功专业人士就应该如此。

sents.en: Lupu and Ruiz-Castro looked at those who rejected the long hours and they found that those workers actually had strikingly similar strategies for maintaining their work-life balance.
sents.cn: 卢普和鲁伊斯-卡斯特罗研究了那些拒绝长时间工作的人，她们发现这些员工在维持工作与生活平衡方面实际上有着惊人相似的策略。

sents.en: They had a tendency to reflect and question assumptions in the name of self-awareness and regularly took steps to adjust the things standing in their way to work-life balance.
sents.cn: 他们倾向于以自我觉察之名反思并质疑固有假设，并定期采取措施来调整那些阻碍他们实现工作与生活平衡的因素。

sents.en: Lupu and Ruiz-Castro identified five steps that the respondents in the study who had better work-life balance used in their jobs.
sents.cn: 卢普和鲁伊斯-卡斯特罗找出了研究中工作与生活平衡较好的受访者在工作中使用的五个步骤。

sents.en: First, they paused and reconsidered beliefs such as "I'm a professional, so I should work, work, work", and asked themselves questions like, "What's currently causing me stress?" Second, after identifying the cause, they zeroed in on their resultant emotions.
sents.cn: 第一，他们会停顿并重新审视诸如"我是专业人士，所以应该工作、工作、工作"这样的观念，并问自己"目前是什么让我感到压力？

sents.en: Did they feel angry, sad, energised?
sents.cn: "第二，在找出原因后，他们聚焦于由此产生的情绪：感到愤怒、悲伤还是充满干劲？

sents.en: Third, they reprioritised, asking "Is working long hours really worth cutting back on family time?", for example.
sents.cn: 第三，他们重新排序优先级，例如问"长时间工作真的值得牺牲家庭时间吗？

sents.en: Fourth, they considered their alternatives: is there anything at work that could be changed to accommodate these new priorities?
sents.cn: "第四，他们考虑替代方案：工作中是否有可以调整以配合这些新优先级的事项？

sents.en: And finally, they implemented changes, like asking their supervisor for greater flexibility, or deciding not to take on every project that comes their way.
sents.cn: 最后，他们落实改变，比如向主管要求更大的灵活性，或决定不接手找上门的每一个项目。

sents.en: This five-step process is something anyone can adopt.
sents.cn: 这一五步流程任何人都可以采用。

sents.en: Going through the steps, and constantly checking in with yourself can help you shift and adapt your professional life to something that will better harmonise with your personal one.
sents.cn: 经历这些步骤并不断检视自我，能帮助你转变并调整职业生涯，使其与个人生活更好地协调。

sents.en: "Awareness of your emotional state is essential in order to determine the changes you want to make in your work and in your life," says Lupu.
sents.cn: "要决定在工作与生活中做出哪些改变，觉察自己的情绪状态至关重要，"卢普说。

sents.en: New York University's Lechner agrees that finding that balance is an ongoing pursuit.
sents.cn: 纽约大学的莱希纳也认为，找到那种平衡是一项持续的追求。

sents.en: It's not simply about dividing up the hours in your day between work, the gym, kids and chores.
sents.cn: 它不只是把你一天中的时间分配在工作、健身房、孩子和家务之间。

sents.en: If the underlying emotional sources of stress are still there, then the time you actually spend at home may not be enjoyable.
sents.cn: 如果压力的根本情绪来源仍在，那么你在家里实际度过的时光可能并不愉快。

sents.en: "We come home and even though physically we are there, mentally we still may be processing things that happened at work.
sents.cn: "我们回到家，尽管身体在那儿，精神上却可能仍在处理工作中发生的事。

sents.en: We're not present," she says.
sents.cn: 我们并不'在场'，"她说。

sents.en: What we call "work-life balance" is actually just a substitute to having a sense of fulfillment and contentment.
sents.cn: 我们所谓的"工作与生活的平衡"，其实只是获得满足与安适感的一种替代品。

sents.en: Of course, finding that balance probably shouldn't be something you have to do by yourself.
sents.cn: 当然，找到那种平衡或许不该是你必须独自完成的事。

sents.en: Research by Erin Kelly, professor of work and organisation studies at MIT, shows companies and managers can play a key role in creating a better environment for workers.
sents.cn: 麻省理工学院工作与组织研究教授艾琳∙凯利的研究表明，公司和经理在为员工创造更好环境方面能起到关键作用。

sents.en: For her book Overload: How Good Jobs Went Bad and What to Do about It, she and co-author Phyllis Moen split more than 1,000 employees at a Fortune 500 company into two groups, one that worked under a management redesign and one that continued working within the existing management structure.
sents.cn: 在为她的著作《过载：好工作如何变坏及应对之道》所做的研究中，她和合著者菲利斯∙莫恩将一家财富500强企业的1,000多名员工分成两组，一组在管理重构下工作，另一组继续在原有管理架构中工作。

sents.en: Under the management redesign, many steps were taken to ensure better work-life balance and prevent burnout (精疲力竭).
sents.cn: 在管理重构下，采取了许多措施以确保更好的工作与生活平衡并防止职业倦怠（精疲力竭）。

sents.en: Managers were regularly reminded to explicitly support their employees.
sents.cn: 经理们被定期提醒要明确表示支持员工。

sents.en: Workers were allowed to make changes, like cancelling 9 am meetings.
sents.cn: 员工被允许做出改变，比如取消上午9点的会议。

sents.en: All of this was done in the name of increasing job satisfaction and giving workers greater flexibility, and to assure workers that it was something management was committed to.
sents.cn: 所有这一切都是为了提高工作满意度、给予员工更大灵活性，并向员工保证这是管理层所承诺的。

sents.en: Unsurprisingly, Kelly and Moen found that employees in the redesign group reported less stress and less burnout.
sents.cn: 不出所料，凯利和莫恩发现，重构组的员工压力更小、倦怠更少。

sents.en: They were less likely to quit their jobs; indeed, over the next four years, they were 40% less likely to quit than those who kept working under the old policies.
sents.cn: 他们离职的可能性更低；事实上，在接下来的四年里，他们离职的可能性比那些继续在旧政策下工作的人低40%。

sents.en: "Work-life balance is understood to be an individual's response, so people think 'it's up to me to manage the craziness of my work life'", says Kelly.
sents.cn: "工作与生活的平衡被认为是个人的应对方式，所以人们认为'管理我工作生活的混乱是自己的事'，"凯利说。

sents.en: But organisations need to examine the demands they're placing on employees.
sents.cn: 但组织需要审视它们对员工提出的要求。

sents.en: "The root problem is not how the two pieces of work and life come together.
sents.cn: "根本问题不在于工作与生活这两部分如何结合，而在于我们对工作侧被要求做的事抱有不合实际的期待。

sents.en: It's that we have unrealistic expectations of what we're asked to do on the work side." If your workplace isn't an environment where work-life balance is possible in the first place, any effort you attempt to make toward it on a personal level will be in vain.
sents.cn: "如果你的职场本身就不是能实现工作与生活平衡的环境，那么你在个人层面为此所做的任何努力都将徒劳。

sents.en: That's a conversation that appears to be gathering pace.
sents.cn: 那是一场似乎正在加速的讨论。

sents.en: The new prevalence of remote and flexible working models will likely all play important roles in how we balance our professional and personal lives.
sents.cn: 远程与灵活办公模式的新近普及，很可能会在我们如何平衡职业与个人生活方面发挥重要作用。

sents.en: And if it seems like finding that perfect balance remains difficult to achieve, the experts say that keeping some perspective can help.
sents.cn: 而如果看起来找到那种完美平衡依然难以实现，专家说保持一定的视角会有所帮助。

sents.en: For millions of people, work is about being able to put food on the table.
sents.cn: 对数百万人而言，工作是为了能够有饭吃。

sents.en: Talking about work-life balance "is a very privileged conversation", says Lechner.
sents.cn: 谈论工作与生活的平衡"是一场非常享有特权的对话"，莱希纳说。

sents.en: "If we're reflecting, maybe we should also reflect on that."
sents.cn: "如果我们在反思，也许我们也该对此反思。"
